title: Whole Reflexed-Sepal and Pendant-Bell Flower
description: One newly authored complete static pendant-bell flowering shoot. A continuous slim stem arches over to a downward hanging flower, with two whole pointed opposite-direction stem leaves. Four long thick outer sepals extend outward then genuinely turn back upward around a short downward open bell-like inner corolla. The inner corolla is a thick closed shell with a real downward mouth and recessed top, surrounding a long central hanging column and three slim whole hanging filaments. This outer upward-reflexed crown and inner short hanging bell are not a broad upright hibiscus cup rotated downward or a daffodil corona recoloured. Whole new stem curve, leaf surfaces, curved sepal profiles and bell cavity. One plant model zero scenes; stylised static appearance only, no exact cultivar, species, reproductive anatomy, growth, roots, pollination, toxicity or ecological function claim.
